new_findings.text: The XOR key for the five obfuscated Android resource blobs is NOT one constant - it is the SECOND CHARACTER of the resource's filename, so every blob has its own key. ResourceManager.as:186 passes 'resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1)' into decryptByteArray, and :41 lists the five filenames. That yields shs3resource.swf -> 'h' = 104, musicresource.swf -> 'u' = 117, soundresource.swf -> 'o' = 111, imageresource.swf -> 'm' = 109, bgresource.swf -> 'g' = 103. This reconciles the two keys the Stage-0 brief already carries (C1's 109 from Mobile.as:352 and C3's 111 for the sound blob) and predicts the other three. Also note decryptByteArray only touches bytes 3..255 (swapping every i%11==0 byte with i+256), which is why the files still begin with a readable 'CWS' magic.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ResourceManager.as:41,186,200-214; verified by decrypting reference/extracted/android/115_Mobile_SHS3Resource.bin at key 104 -> valid CWS v17 SWF, 1,040,849 bytes inflated, 1,912 SymbolClass entries
new_findings.quote: ResourceManager.as:41 `internal static var resourceFileNameArray:Array = ["shs3resource.swf","musicresource.swf","soundresource.swf","imageresource.swf","bgresource.swf"];` :186 `ba = decryptByteArray(ba,resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1));` :205 `for(var i:int = 3; i < 256; i++)` :207 `if(i % 11 == 0)` :213 `ba[i] ^= key;`
new_findings.lane_impact: Cross-lane extraction rule (art, audio, items): keys are 104/117/111/109/103 by resource, derived not guessed - anyone opening the remaining blobs can stop brute-forcing.

new_findings.text: A zero-hit grep for a SOURCE-LEVEL identifier over reference/decompiled/shs3_payload is not evidence that the web build lacks the feature, because the web payload's class, method and field names are obfuscated to §1tNNNNs0§ forms. Proven in this packet twice over: android's getSellAmt is §1t546s0§ in the web build, android Item.as's modifier constants are §1t8734s0§..§1t8741s0§, and android NodeGenerator.isNoChangeTown is §1t70s0§.§1t1140s0§. Web-side absence must be argued from a structural signature (imports + literal constants + call shape), the method actually used to pin §1t1712s0§ and §1t8702s0§ in this same packet - never from a name grep.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t17s0§.as:1977 (= android Item.as:1582 getSellAmt); §1t70s0§.as:407-415 (= android NodeGenerator.as:393-400 isNoChangeTown); §1t17s0§.as:18-22 (= android Item.as:8-16 modifier ids)

new_findings.lane_impact: Gauntlet-wide method rule: 'ZERO hits under shs3_payload' may be quoted as the state of the evidence, never as a finding that the web build lacks the thing.
